## Historical audit — S0246

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/audit_sources/raw_failures/scene_rsi_v2_1/r2/scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/test/commons_189918915/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL line and character ranges.

| Aspect | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The explicit task was to reconstruct an indoor scene from one RGB image, matching geometry, materials, camera and framing using separate meshes; no reference-image projection or external files were allowed (line 1, chars [0,8733)). The student’s inventory *interpreted* the scene as a high warehouse aisle with pallet racks, wrapped loads, ceiling strips and a skylight. The reference image itself is not visible in this audit, so that interpretation is not independently confirmed (line 3, chars [0,12731)). |
| Actual construction | The student supplied a complete program and the runner attempted it: architecture, two racks, multiple pallet-load assets, roof fixtures and skylight; rails, braces, crossbars, runners and deck pieces were positioned as connections and supports. These are code-level constructions, not verified visible connections. Seeded placement and selected empty bays controlled repetition (lines 3–4, chars [0,12731) and [0,13375)). |
| Materials and view | The program specified colored surfaces, carton noise/bump, film roughness, emissive fixtures, area lights, a 24 mm camera with 12° roll, Cycles settings and compositor glow. Their actual appearance, lighting, framing and pose relative to the reference remain unverified (lines 3–4, same ranges). No actual camera or render defect can be diagnosed from the visible record. |
| Validation and outcome | Step 1 timed out after approximately 490 seconds; `ok` was false, stdout and stderr were empty, and image was null (line 5, chars [0,1084)). **Technical interruption; visual and geometric outcome unknown.** The trace does not establish whether scene creation or rendering was the time-consuming phase, nor a successful build, partial visual correctness, algorithm failure or empty patch. No correction or second execution is recorded. |
| Teacher and exploration | This is a student trajectory. No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, input or adoption is recorded. The student independently produced one program; the session reports zero tool calls before execution, with no visible iterative exploration or render comparison (line 2, chars [0,2863); lines 3–5). |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, a successful visual comparison requires an actual render; code, object names and intended connections do not establish appearance or correctness. Here, the dense repeated rack and load geometry is a possible contributor to the timeout, but the empty logs do not establish its cause. The warehouse interpretation, object coverage, materials, connection quality, camera and light match all remain unresolved without the reference and a completed render.
